questions.question: A block of wood is placed in a tub of water, and its top half remains visible above the water level. What can we say about the whole block?
options: Only the top half is floating
Only the submerged half is floating
The whole block is floating
The block is sinking slowly

questions.question: A toy boat floats perfectly in a shallow tray filled with 5 cm of water. If the boat is moved to a deep swimming pool, how will its floating behaviour change?
options: It will float much higher because there is more water underneath
It will float at the exact same level because depth does not affect how well it floats
It will sink to the bottom because the water pressure is greater
It will tip over easily due to the increased depth of the liquid

questions.question: Under what condition will a shaped object, like a hollow metal bowl, float in water?
options: If its shape allows it to push aside a volume of water that has a mass equal to its own mass without submerging completely
If it is made of a material that is completely waterproof and cannot absorb any liquid
If the air trapped inside the bowl has a greater mass than the metal itself
If it has a perfectly flat bottom to distribute the downward gravitational force

questions.question: Approximately how much upward force is required to lift a 1 kg bag of flour vertically on Earth?
options: 1 N

questions.question: How many grams are there in a standard mass of 1 kilogram?
Which of the following formulas correctly shows how to calculate the gravitational force (weight, W) acting on an object?
options: W = m $$\div$$ g
W = g $$\div$$ m
W = m $$\times$$ g
W = m + g

questions.question: If a spring extends by 2 cm when a force of 1 N is added, how much further will it extend when a second, identical 1 N force is added (within its elastic limit)?
options: It will extend by another 2 cm
It will extend by another 1 cm
It will extend by another 4 cm
It will not extend any further

questions.question: What does it mean to say that the extension of a spring is directly proportional to the force applied?
options: As the force increases, the extension decreases by the same ratio
Doubling the force results in doubling the extension of the spring
The extension remains constant regardless of how much force is applied
The spring will permanently deform as soon as any force is applied

questions.question: Why is a steel spring described as being elastic?
options: It can be stretched to many times its original length without breaking
It returns to its original length once the stretching force is removed
It becomes stiffer and harder to stretch the more force you apply to it
It conducts electricity when it is stretched out

questions.question: Which of the following describes a key mechanical function of a lever when used as a force multiplier?
options: It reduces the distance the load travels to zero
It multiplies a small input force into a larger output force
It decreases the force needed by increasing the mass of the object
It eliminates the need for a pivot point

questions.question: How do the different types of levers mainly differ from one another?
options: They are made of different materials like wood, plastic, or metal
They have the pivot, load, and effort in different relative positions
Some require gravity to work while others do not
They can only be used to lift objects of different weights

questions.question: What is the correct formula used to calculate pressure?
options: Pressure = force $$\times$$ area
Pressure = area $$\div$$ force
Pressure = force $$\div$$ area
Pressure = force + area

questions.question: What is another name for the unit of pressure 'newtons per square metre' (N/m$$^2$$)?
options: Joule (J)
Watt (W)
Pascal (Pa)
Newton (N)

questions.question: Why does a deep-sea diver experience much greater pressure at a depth of 100 metres than at 10 metres?
options: The water is colder at greater depths, which squeezes the diver more
There is a greater weight of liquid pushing down from above at that depth
The density of the water decreases as you go deeper
The gravitational pull is significantly stronger at the bottom of the ocean

questions.question: Why does atmospheric pressure decrease as an airplane climbs higher into the sky?
options: The air is moving much faster at higher altitudes
The temperature drops, causing the air molecules to disappear
There is less air above the airplane pushing down
The Earth's gravity becomes zero at typical flight altitudes

questions.question: How does the stretching behaviour of a rubber band differ from that of a standard metal spring?
options: The rubber band does not extend at all when a force is applied
The extension of a rubber band increases by different amounts for each equal sized increase in force
The rubber band extends by the exact same amount for every equal addition of force
The rubber band can only extend when it is heated up

questions.question: What happens to the microscopic particles inside a solid floor when a very heavy cabinet is placed on it?
options: The particles expand in size to support the weight
The particles are squashed closer together
The particles start sliding past one another and become liquid
The particles disappear to make room for the cabinet

questions.question: How do you calculate the moment of a force?
options: Moment = force $$\div$$ perpendicular distance from the pivot
Moment = force $$\times$$ perpendicular distance from the pivot
Moment = force + perpendicular distance from the pivot
Moment = perpendicular distance $$\div$$ force
